content: The role of corticosteroids in the process of labour is not well understood. Animal studies have demonstrated that cortisol secretion by the fetal adrenal gland plays a critical role in initiating labour in sheep. Additionally, the infusion of glucocorticosteroids into the fetus has been shown to induce premature labour in sheep. Based on these findings, it has been hypothesized that corticosteroids may facilitate the induction of labour in women. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effects of corticosteroids for cervical ripening or induction of labour during the third trimester, comparing their efficacy with other established methods of cervical priming or labour induction. To gather relevant data, the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group Trials Register was searched in December 2005, and bibliographies of pertinent studies were reviewed. This search was updated on July 16, 2009, with the results added to the awaiting classification section. The review included clinical trials that investigated the use of corticosteroids for cervical ripening or labour induction in the third trimester. A systematic approach was employed to manage the large volume and complexity of trial data related to labour induction. This involved a two-stage data extraction process. The quality of the trials was assessed, and study authors were contacted for additional information. Adverse effects reported in the trials were also collected. Only one small trial, involving 66 women, met the inclusion criteria. The primary outcome, vaginal birth within 24 hours, was not reported in this trial. The study found no significant benefit of intramuscular corticosteroids combined with intravenous oxytocin compared to the use of oxytocin alone. However, due to the small sample size of this trial, these findings should be interpreted with caution. The authors concluded that the effectiveness of corticosteroids for labour induction remains uncertain. This method is not commonly used for labour induction, and further research in this area is likely unnecessary. It is worth noting that seven citations in the awaiting classification section of the review may influence the conclusions once they are assessed.
